cli.description:
Subtitles (spoken language + target languages) for a video or playlist address (YouTube, Dailymotion,
PeerTube, Arte…),  a video file or all the videos of a folder, from the command line.

    python -m subtitles <video or playlist address | video file | folder | .batch.json file> [options]

A folder becomes a project, as in the web interface: a dl-sub-dub.project.json file is written as the work goes, and
running the same command again after an interruption resumes where the project stopped. A playlist is downloaded
into a folder of its own, then processed as a project.

Web interface: python -m subtitles.web (see README). Settings come from config.toml overridden by
%LOCALAPPDATA%/subtitles/config.json (written by the web interface); the options below take precedence.
cli.idle: minutes without activity before stopping (default: [web] idle_min, 60; 0 = never)
cli.lang: language of the messages ({langs}); default: ui_language setting, else the system language
cli.list: show the configured engines and exit
cli.new_project: folder: ignore the existing project file and start again from the folder inventory
cli.no_subfolders: folder: only the videos of the folder itself
cli.open: open the page in the browser
cli.output: output folder (downloaded video, .srt; intermediate files in .travail/)
cli.playlist: address of a video in a playlist: download the whole playlist and process it as a project
cli.port: listening port (default: [web] port of the configuration, 4420)
cli.redo: redo the transcription and the translation even if they exist
cli.source: one or more video or playlist addresses (YouTube, Dailymotion, PeerTube, Arte…), a .txt file with one address per line (several addresses: one project), or the path of a video file, of a folder (project) or of a .batch.json file
cli.spoken: spoken language (en, de…) if the detection is wrong
cli.targets: comma-separated target languages (fr,en…); default: target_languages setting
cli.transcription: id of a transcription server from the configuration
cli.translator: id of a translator from the configuration (local, claude, none…)
cli.until: folder: last step (default: translation; dubbing, or mux to assemble an MKV)
dialog.source_folder: Folder of the videos to subtitle
engine.none: No translation (subtitles in the spoken language)

ui.tip.default_language: The language spoken in your videos, offered for each new project (two-letter code: fr, en, ja…). Left empty, it is recognised video by video, which works well in general. Setting it avoids a mistake on a very short video, or one that mixes several languages.
ui.tip.chunk: Subtitles are sent to the translator in batches, with the two previous ones as context. A larger batch makes fewer requests and gives more context (more consistent), but if the model loses a line, the whole batch is done again. 25 suits most models; lower it to 10-15 for a small local model that often slips.
ui.tip.idle: The service stops by itself after this many minutes doing nothing (no work under way, no action on the page), to free the memory. Start it again to go on. 0: it never stops by itself.
ui.tip.max_height: The highest picture quality to download (1080p = Full HD). A video only available smaller is taken as it is. Higher: a sharper picture, but much larger files (an hour in 4K weighs about 6 GB, against 1.5 GB in 1080p). Can also be set per project and per video.
ui.tip.ytdlp_extra: Options given to yt-dlp (the tool that downloads the videos) for every download, separated by spaces. A useful one: --cookies-from-browser firefox, for videos that need you to be signed in to your account (with some browsers, Chrome for example, close it first). Leave empty if you do not need any.
ui.tip.speed: How many seconds of video this server transcribes in one second (for example 16: an hour of video in a little under 4 minutes). Only used to announce the time before running. It is a starting value: the service replaces it with what it measures, video after video.
ui.tip.command: Only for a transcription server installed on this PC that you do not keep running: the command that starts it (a JSON list, for example ["python", "D:/transcription/server.py"]). The service starts it when a transcription needs it and stops it along with itself. Leave empty for a server always on, here or on another machine.
ui.tip.effort: Claude only: how long the model thinks before translating. "low" is enough for ordinary subtitles; "medium" or "high" take more care of puns, names and tone, but each translation is slower and costs more.
ui.tip.review_effort: For Claude only: how much the model thinks when it reviews a transcription (names, full review). Higher, it finds more mistakes in a difficult dialogue, and costs more: the thinking counts in the output tokens.
ui.tip.supervision: If your local AI (llama.cpp…) is started and stopped by a supervision service, its address (for example http://127.0.0.1:8300). dl-sub-dub then asks it to start the AI when a translation needs it, and to stop it before the dubbing to free the graphics card. Leave empty if the AI runs all the time.
ui.tip.stop_after: Ticked: the local AI is stopped as soon as the translation is over, which gives back its memory and the graphics card (useful if you play or dub next). Unticked: it stays loaded, and the next video starts faster.
ui.tip.clean_audio: Clean the audio extracts: ticked, the soundtrack taken out of each video for the transcription is deleted at the end of each task and with "Clean now" (also when a video is cancelled or stopped). Advised: it is the largest file of the working folder, and it is made again in a few seconds if needed. What a stopped dubbing left goes with it. Unticked: it is kept.
ui.tip.clean_subtitles: Clean the subtitle copies: ticked, the working copies of the subtitles (.srt, .vtt) in the working folder are deleted at the end of each task and with "Clean now". The subtitles next to your videos, the ones your players use, are never deleted. Unticked: the copies are kept.
ui.tip.clean_transcription: Clean the transcriptions and translations: ticked, the transcribed text (transcription.json) and the translations (translation.<language>.json) are deleted at the end of each task and with "Clean now". Not advised: keeping them lets you later add a language, change the layout of the subtitles or redo a dubbing without transcribing or translating again (so without paying an API again); they are small.
ui.tip.clean_logs: Clean the logs: ticked, the logs of the tasks (what happened, the errors; a few KB each) older than the age chosen below are deleted at the end of each task and with "Clean now". Ticked or not, these old logs are also deleted each time the service starts.
ui.tip.clean_dubbing: Clean the dubbed voices: ticked, the dubbed voice of each language (the file dubbing/<language>.m4a of the working folder) is deleted at the end of each task and with "Clean now". Nothing is lost for watching: the final MKV already holds this voice. But to make that MKV again or add a track to it, the whole dubbing must be done again (minutes of graphics card per video). Unticked (advised if you have the space): it is kept.
ui.tip.work_limit: So that the working folder (.work) does not grow forever: past this age (in days) or this total size (in MB), the working folders of the oldest videos are deleted whole, transcription included. This happens when the service starts and with "Clean now". Your videos, their subtitles and the MKVs are never touched, nor a folder in use. 0: no limit.
ui.tip.target_languages: The languages you want subtitles in, offered for each new project. Two-letter codes separated by commas, for example: fr, en, es. Subtitles in the spoken language are always made as well; a language equal to the spoken one is simply skipped.
ui.tip.dub_wsl: Tick it if the command of the dubbing goes through WSL, the Linux built into Windows (it then starts with wsl): the paths of the files are given to it in their Linux form (D:/Videos becomes /mnt/d/Videos).
ui.tip.dub_command: The Python of the environment where the dubbing engine (OmniVoice) is installed, as a JSON list. On Linux or macOS: ["/home/me/dl-sub-dub-dubbing/.venv/bin/python"]. On Windows with WSL: ["wsl", "-d", "Ubuntu", "--", "/home/me/dl-sub-dub-dubbing/.venv/bin/python"], with the WSL box ticked. See "Dubbing" in the README to install it.
ui.tip.dub_model: The voice model used for the dubbing: either a Hugging Face identifier (for example k2-fsa/OmniVoice, downloaded by itself the first time, about 3 GB), or the path of a folder where the model is already saved.
ui.tip.dub_steps: For each sentence, the voice is generated then refined in several passes. More passes: a cleaner, more natural voice, but a longer dubbing, roughly in proportion. 32 (the default) is a good balance; 16 is about twice as fast with a slightly less clean voice; above 32, the difference is barely heard.
ui.tip.cpl: The largest number of characters on a line of subtitle (spaces included). 42 is the standard of television and video platforms; shorter, subtitles are easier to read but change more often.
ui.tip.lines: The largest number of lines shown at once for a subtitle. 2 is the usual; 1 hides less of the picture but subtitles go by faster.
ui.tip.max_duration: The longest time the same subtitle stays on screen, in seconds. A longer sentence is cut into several subtitles. 6 seconds is the usual.
ui.tip.min_duration: The shortest time a subtitle is shown, even a single word ("Yes."), so that there is time to see it. 1 second is the usual.
ui.tip.gap: When the speaker pauses at least this long (in seconds), the sentence is cut there into two subtitles. Smaller: shorter subtitles that follow the rhythm of the speech better; larger: longer blocks.
ui.tip.cps: The reading speed assumed, in characters per second: each subtitle stays on screen at least the time to read it at that speed. 17 suits adults; lower it (12 to 15) for children or for subtitles in a language being learnt.
v2.tip.spoken: The language spoken in these videos. "Automatic detection" recognises it for each video, which works well in general. Choosing the language avoids a mistake on a very short video, or one that mixes several languages.
v2.tip.next_to: The subtitles are saved next to each video, with the same name (my video.fr.srt next to my video.mp4). VLC and most players then find them by themselves.
v2.tip.copies: As well, a copy of the subtitles goes into the output folder chosen in the Settings, for example to find them all in one place.
v2.tip.named: Ticked: the project goes into a subfolder with its name, inside the folder chosen (handy to keep projects apart). Unticked: its files go straight into the folder chosen.
err.disk_full: Not enough space on the disk of {folder}: about {need} GB free are needed, {free} are left. Free some space (Settings, Clean now) or choose another folder.

ytdlp.hint_pip: installed with pip, pipx or Homebrew: run “pipx upgrade yt-dlp”, “python -m pip install -U yt-dlp” or “brew upgrade yt-dlp” as the case may be.
ytdlp.hint_source: run from its sources: “git pull” in its folder.
ytdlp.hint_package: installed by the package manager of the system: update it with that (for example “sudo apt upgrade yt-dlp”), or install the official build, which updates itself.
err.ytdlp_downloading: A download is under way: yt-dlp will be updated once the downloads are over.

v2.ytdlp.failed_download: A download failed. yt-dlp {version} is {days} days old: a newer version often fixes this kind of error.
v2.ytdlp.updated: yt-dlp is up to date: version {version}.

ui.tip.chunks_at_once: How many chunks of subtitles of the same video are sent together to the translator. 1 (the default): one after the other, each with the end of the previous one, translated, as context. 2 or 3: faster if the server can handle several requests at the same time (llama.cpp started with --parallel 2 or 3, or an API); the context of chunks sent together is then the original text before them. No real use if the server handles only one at a time.
v2.dub.replace_confirm: For each video of this project, once its MKV is made and checked (every track, same duration), the original video will go to the recycle bin and the MKV will take its place, under the same name.
